Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Oh, yes... He sits way too close to the television when watching cartoons, and even when reading books, he holds them right up to his face. I'm always telling him to move back a bit, but he just gets so absorbed in what he's doing.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Well, sometimes I notice he asks me to repeat things multiple times. It's like he didn't quite catch what I said the first time around. But once I repeat it, he seems to understand perfectly fine.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: His teeth... they're just so fragile! Even with gentle brushing, we've had instances where they've chipped or broken. It's really worrying because I want to make sure he has healthy teeth as he grows older.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Yes... There's this structural issue with his heart that the doctors have been monitoring since birth. We go for regular check-ups to ensure everything is okay, and the medical team has been wonderful in keeping us updated on his condition.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Coordination seems to be a bit of an issue for him. When he tries to run or play sports, he can appear less graceful than his peers. Not drastically so, but noticeable enough that I've wondered if maybe there's something more going on that needs attention.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Feeding was a real challenge when he was younger. He would spit up a lot and just seemed to have trouble keeping food down. Thankfully, as he's grown, that's become much less of an issue.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Developmentally, he seems to lag behind his peers. And speech... oh, it's been a journey. Sometimes his words aren't clear, and I have to really listen closely to understand what he's trying to communicate. It breaks my heart to see him struggle, but we're working through it together.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural issue with his heart that has been monitored since birth, requiring regular check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experienced feeding difficulties as a baby, including spitting up and trouble keeping food down, although this has improved with age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has coordination issues, appearing less graceful than his peers during physical activities, and has experienced developmental delays.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and many have developmental delays ranging from mild to severe.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing difficulties, often asking for repetition and showing signs of not fully catching what is said the first time around.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience conductive hearing loss, often due to recurrent otitis media or glue ear, and may require hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sits very close to the television and holds books close to his face, indicating potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, including astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has fragile teeth that chip or break easily, even with gentle brushing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences developmental delays and speech difficulties, which may impact his educational progress.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome often require extra help in school and may need to transfer to special schooling or have Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays, speech difficulties, and coordination issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, including autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, and anxiety, and may experience developmental delays.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved fingers, and an increased curvature of the spine.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and address any dental concerns.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight review to assess for vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart condition.
* Consideration of a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to assess for skeletal anomalies.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to address developmental delays and coordination issues.
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural heart abnormality that requires regular monitoring by cardiologists to ensure the condition remains stable.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulty digesting certain foods and occasional discomfort after eating, suggesting gastrointestinal issues that may require dietary adjustments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties are common in children with KBG syndrome, with some requiring short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds, and a very small number needing longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was developmentally slower to reach certain milestones like walking or sitting but is making progress with support and therapy. Additionally, the patient has scoliosis, which affects her posture.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is common in KBG syndrome, with the degree of delay ranging from mild to severe, and some individuals may experience seizures, with around 20-40% of people reported to have seizures of varying types.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble hearing certain sounds, particularly in noisy environments, and has required regular hearing reviews.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience hearing loss, often due to recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing the board at school and often squints or leans forward to get a better look, indicating vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel on several teeth, making them more susceptible to cavities, and requires regular dental check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns are common, including weak enamel, and regular dental check-ups are recommended, particularly with a specialist SEN dentist for those with significant sensory issues.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's vision and hearing difficulties have affected her performance in class, and she may require additional support.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with some attending mainstream primary school and others requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and requires support and therapy to catch up in many areas.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis, which affects her posture, and is working with physical therapists to improve her spinal alignment.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may experience delayed closure of the soft spot on their head or hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental concerns
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor hearing and address any concerns
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess and address vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart condition
* Skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to monitor skeletal development and address any concerns
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental delays and behavioural differences
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consideration of review and investigation for tethered cord if clinical concerns arise

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect that is being monitored regularly to see how it develops.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a strong feeding aversion to certain textures and tastes, and mealtime can be frustrating at times because of this. There are also palatal abnormalities that are being monitored closely.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds. A very small number of children have required longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Physical activities seem to tire the patient out more easily than her peers, and even simple play can leave her exhausted after a short while.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported as having seizures, of varying types. Seizures typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes seems to hear certain sounds but not others, and does not always respond to sounds from another room.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sits very close to the TV when watching her favorite shows and also when reading books, indicating possible vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty chewing harder foods like apples or carrots, and meal times have had to be adjusted to ensure she can handle what's on her plate.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school. The extra demands of mainstream secondary school may prove too challenging, and children may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine. Many people with KBG syndrome have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor dental concerns such as weak enamel and large front teeth.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight review to monitor for vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor for heart conditions.
* Consider a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to monitor for skeletal abnormalities.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support the patient's development and address any behavioural differences.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular heart check-ups due to a pre-existing condition. The cardiologist keeps a close eye on her, and updates are received on her condition regularly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes. Some may require surgery, while others just need monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often refuses to eat certain foods, which can make mealtime challenging. Introducing a variety of foods slowly is being worked on to expand her palate.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds. A lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient appears less coordinated when moving compared to her peers. Physical therapy is being considered to help improve her motor skills and coordination.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, of varying types. Seizures typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to turn the TV volume up very high. Hearing tests have shown everything to be fine, but she prefers louder sounds for some reason.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss. Many children have required multiple aeration tube (grommet) insertions to relieve pressure inside the ear, and some have still required hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which means she needs glasses to correct her vision. Finding frames she likes has been a challenge, but they are managing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint. Treatment can include patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery to bring the eyes into line.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: Chewing harder foods can be difficult for her. Adapting her diet and ensuring regular dental check-ups are being done to prevent any further issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel. Careful brushing is very important, and regular dental check-ups are recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school. The extra demands of mainstream secondary school may prove too challenging, and children may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety. Medication(s) may be appropriate in some circumstances.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with hip dysplasia, and regular check-ups with the orthopedic specialist have helped stay on top of her condition and adjust treatments as needed.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis). Many people have short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly). A small number of children have had hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to prevent further dental issues
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review
* Check position of testes in boys
* Consider a palate review (particularly if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns)
* Referral for a cardiac review (including echo and ECG) following diagnosis
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) in children following diagnosis
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural abnormality in her heart, which is monitored regularly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences feeding difficulties and can be frustrated during mealtimes if food isn't prepared just right, sometimes refusing to eat altogether.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient occasionally has episodes where she stares off into space and seems completely blank, not responding to anything around her for a few seconds, before snapping back to normal.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to turn the TV volume very high, suggesting potential hearing issues, and has required regular hearing reviews.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has mentioned that things look blurry to her, especially when trying to focus on something far away, indicating potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel, which her dentist has pointed out, and she is working on taking good care of her teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel and large front teeth.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with shorter fingers than typical, which has presented challenges with gripping small objects or using certain toys.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address weak enamel and other dental concerns.
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor for potential hearing loss.
* Eyesight review to assess and address any vision problems.
* Cardiac review to monitor the structural abnormality in the heart.
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to address developmental delays and challenges.
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Regular check-ups with a specialist to monitor and address any other medical concerns, such as seizures or skeletal issues.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tiredness more quickly than other kids his age, even after simple play, suggesting potential cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had feeding difficulties as a baby, often spitting up or showing signs of discomfort after eating.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has seizures that started around his third birthday and has been working with neurologists to manage them since then.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had otitis media last year and has had to visit the doctor several times for treatment.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains of blurry vision, especially when trying to focus on something far away.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth seem to break or chip very easily, requiring several visits to the dentist for repairs.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel, and careful brushing is very important, with regular dental check-ups recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is behind other children in development, both physically and cognitively, which is being monitored closely with his healthcare team.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with many attending mainstream primary school but potentially transferring to special schooling or requiring Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with clarity when trying to talk and takes a while to get his words out, and is behind other children in development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may have learning difficulties.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and address any issues promptly.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to check for any signs of conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight review to assess for any vision problems such as astigmatism or squint.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to check for any heart conditions.
* Consideration of a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to assess for any skeletal anomalies.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy as needed to support development and manage any behavioral differences.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences bowel problems and accidents.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired quickly when running around or playing sports.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some may have developmental delay and learning difficulties.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had fluid in his ear at times.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which means his eyes turn inward slightly.

* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support developmental delay and behavioral differences.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient had otitis media last year, which was a scary and painful experience.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia (far-sightedness) and needs regular glasses adjustments, which affects her daily life.
